video.title: The Points League Bust You Can’t Ignore

summary: Josh Lloyd goes through points league busts on Yahoo and ESPN. These are players he thinks are ranked or drafted too high for points formats, as of September 21. A bust does not mean you never draft the player. It means the market is valuing him wrongly. He keeps comparing each player's current rank and ADP with where he finished in points leagues last season, and he says roles and teammates have changed. Big Yahoo busts include Tyrese Maxey, Kevin Durant, Tyrese Haliburton, Chet Holmgren and Kon Knueppel. On ESPN he flags Jalen Johnson, Jalen Brunson, Trae Young, Pascal Siakam and Nikola Vucevic. In the mailbag he says the draft and the waiver wire matter about equally, playoff schedules matter least at draft time, and the whole game is about getting value.

rules.text: Calling a player a bust does not mean you should never draft him. It means the market is valuing him wrongly at his current price.
rules.quote: What does a bust mean? Does it mean you don't draft them? No, that's not what it means.

rules.text: Yahoo rankings are format agnostic, so they do not fit any one format, and ADP tends to follow them. Do not trust them for points leagues.
rules.quote: Yahoo's rankings are format agnostic. They throw an X rank out there. What does it mean?

rules.text: Format matters. A player who is good value in category leagues can be a bust in points leagues.
rules.quote: in a points league. And this is where again format is important in a points league.

rules.text: Players whose Yahoo ranks are boosted by 9-category value are hard to value correctly for points leagues.
rules.quote: these are the guys again that get real nine cap fluffed which creates issues with trying to assign their value for points leagues

rules.text: Not every drafter knows why a player is ranked where he is, so many people get fooled by bad ranks.
rules.quote: not everyone knows why players are in certain positions. So they can get fooled.

rules.text: In points leagues, minutes drive usage, usage drives scoring and scoring drives fantasy points. A player who only scores needs big volume to pay off.
rules.quote: minutes begets usage, usage begets scoring, scoring begets fantasy points.

rules.text: Play the prediction game. Project a realistic stat line for a player and ask whether it would really justify his draft spot.
rules.quote: play the prediction game. What do you think a reasonable predicted stat line is

rules.text: Avoid single-season myopia. Look at more than one past season, for example when comparing games played.
rules.quote: I want you to really be cautious of single season myopia.

rules.text: Last season's finish is not the final word, but it shows how much a player has to improve to justify his rank.
rules.quote: it's a good indication to see how much someone needs to maybe improve to hit this number.

rules.text: ESPN default points scoring penalizes missed shots, so inefficient shooters lose value there.
rules.quote: ESPN default scoring penalizes missed shots.

rules.text: ESPN gives separate points league ranks, but its ADP mixes formats together and does not mean much.
rules.quote: ESPN splits them up. They go, "Here's your points league ranks." Now, they're ADPs.

rules.text: Playoff schedules are the least important factor at draft time. Use them only as a tiebreaker between equal players. Do not take a worse player for a better playoff schedule.
rules.quote: Hey, should I take a worse player who's got a better playoff schedule?" No, you shouldn't.

rules.text: Later in the season, playoff schedules matter through smart streaming and avoiding two-game weeks.
rules.quote: it becomes more important about maxing out through smart streaming, avoiding a twoame week if it's close

rules.text: Hitting on value picks in the draft is probably the biggest factor in winning a league.
rules.quote: Drafting and nailing the value picks is probably the number one thing that contributes to winning.

rules.text: The waiver wire matters as much as the draft. Grab hot players who stay hot, and stream to get a games-played edge in head-to-head.
rules.quote: using it to max out your games in certain spots and taking that games played advantage in a head-to-head format.

rules.text: Overall, the name of the game is value: from the draft, streaming, hot waiver pickups and short-term injury replacements.
rules.quote: the name of the game is value. get value through streaming, hot wave wide pickups, short-term injury replacements
